title: crosslang-sdks-compact-session-model-and-typed-iterables
text:
crosslang-sdks-compact-session-model-and-typed-iterables

description:
Motivation: Engineers have had duplicated session wiring and slightly divergent streaming iterator ergonomics across the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. This led to inconsistent retry behavior and awkward cross-language examples. This PR introduces a compact session model (session v2) plus typed async/pull-stream iterables to harmonize the developer surface across languages and to provide a single place for credential rotation and retry presets.

What this changes: session v2 centralizes holder and lease semantics (lease-grace, lease-renew hooks) and moves the lightweight heartbeat into the connector layer. Streaming APIs now expose typed iterables/pullstreams with explicit resume tokens and a small cancellation token primitive. Retry/backoff presets (low-latency, balanced, high-throughput) are codified and wired into the SDK session factory so clients get consistent defaults. Each SDK receives an ergonomic facade: Python adds AsyncStreamCursor, TypeScript adds AsyncPullIterable<T>, Go adds PullIterator and lightweight ContextCancel helpers.

Compatibility and migration: session v2 is opt-in by default; we keep session v1 shims until the next major bump. There is a migration guide (docs/sdk/migration/session-v2.md) included in this PR; it documents the few API renames and shows before/after snippets. For most users the upgrade is a drop-in change if they use higher-level client helpers (they will get improved reauth/resume automatically).

Implementation notes: - Centralized credential adapter in sdk-core (connector/session/adapter.go|py|ts) with a small, well-documented interface for provider implementations. - Typed iterables implemented with a small adapter layer so existing examples can switch with minimal code. - Retry presets implemented with deterministic jitter and a max-window that respects the session lease. - Added integration tests that drive long-running mock streams and assert resume correctness, bounded token usage, and expected latencies under synthetic batch loads.

Testing and CI: Unit tests added for all three SDKs (python: tests/stream/test_session_v2.py, ts: packages/sdk/tests/stream-session.spec.ts, go: sdk-go/stream/session_v2_test.go). Integration job added to the CI matrix to run cross-sdk smoke tests against the local mock connector. All CI checks passed after two minor flake fixes.

Rollout plan: merge to main, tag SDK packages in the usual order (py -> ts -> go) and publish patch releases. Monitor telemetry for session-connect latency and stream resume rates for the next 48 hours; notify SRE if regressions exceed 10% from baseline.

Follow-ups: - Add a small UX-focused example app that shows multi-language session handoff (ENG-1435). - Consider making session v2 the default after one release cycle and telemetry confirmation. - Explore exposing the typed iterator as an opt-in runtime plugin for older clients.

release_notes:
Python/TS/Go SDKs: introduce compact session model (session v2), typed async iterables for streaming APIs, and coordinated retry/backoff presets. Bumps: py 3.12.0, ts 2.7.0, go v1.5.0. No API surface breaking changes for typical consumers; migration guide included.

review_comments:
Marta Chen: please split the large python test into table-driven cases so flakes are easier to debug — addressed in b2c3d4e
Liam O'Connell: can we avoid exposing low-level lease internals to end users? suggest hiding default lease hooks behind factory options — replied: moved to factory options in a follow-up commit
Priya Nair: nit on TS types: prefer explicit generic on AsyncPullIterable<T> for readability — fixed in c3d4e5f
Security Bot: flagged potential token exposure in example; author updated README to obfuscate tokens and added a note about KMS usage
